hero.headline: A 241 ppm dip every 6.27 days in TIC 261136679, consistent with pi Men c.
hero.accent: A known planet, not a discovery.
hero.lede: 3,485 stored brightness measurements over 26.0 days. The panel, 2 Sentinels and 3 Probes (no people), marked 7 dips, which the vetting code grouped into 3 signals: 1 passed, 1 flagged, 1 rejected.
hero.archive: The stored archive cross-match (the repository's stored copy) finds the lead signal consistent with pi Men c, a published planet: a known planet, not a discovery. Archive values only. This page claims no detection.
hero.qualifier: Each dip is this pipeline's own candidate, unconfirmed as an independent detection; the archive match says the planet is already known, not that this run confirmed it.

star.name: pi Men
star.source: SIMBAD, ICRS J2000 coordinates of the named star (pi Mensae, HD 39091). Used only to place the star on the all-sky map.

dips.subject: tess-fa3483ce6f83

quotes.name: Sentinel · Volunteer
quotes.text: Three similar dips of about 0.0003 depth, each lasting a few hours, recur at roughly 6.3-day spacing (near 1325.4, 1331.8 and 1338.05). The first falls at the start of the data and the last at the end, so the shapes are only partly covered, but the repeat and the depth fit a transit.
quotes.label: potential planet

quotes.name: Sentinel · Skeptic
quotes.text: Three similar flat-bottomed dips about 250-300 ppm deep recur every ~6.3 days, and there is no alternating depth or secondary eclipse. The first and last dips sit at the edges of the data, so they are only partly covered, but the periodic repeat favours a transiting planet.
quotes.label: potential planet

dips.verdict: Passed every vetting check. Its period matches pi Men c in the stored archive cross-match (ΔP 0.08%): a known planet, recovered, not a discovery. The dip itself stays a candidate, unconfirmed as an independent detection.

dips.subject: tess-04b815001aa6

quotes.name: Sentinel · Skeptic
quotes.text: Two short, flat-bottomed dips of about 300 ppm at ~1344.27 and ~1350.45 (spacing ~6.2 d) have matching depth and duration, as expected for a periodic transit. Neither shows a V shape, a secondary eclipse, a ramp or a step, but the data around the second dip is scattered, so I am only moderately conf
quotes.label: potential planet

quotes.name: Sentinel · Volunteer
quotes.text: Two short, sharp drops of about 300 ppm are visible near 1344.4 and 1350.5, each lasting about 3 hours and each made up of several consecutive points. They could be transits, but the scatter is high and increases in the later part of the light curve, so they could also be instrumental.
quotes.label: potential planet

archive.source: NASA Exoplanet Archive, table ps (default_flag = 1), as recorded in docs/results/pi_men_validation.md by scripts/validate_known_planets.py (live archive query, commit 0f6dbdc). Only pi Men c is recorded there, so only pi Men c is listed; its transit mid-time was not recorded, so no per-epoch offset is computed here; the validation note's mean timing offset (−8.0 min over 5 of 5 epochs) is cited instead. Replace it with the output of 'setuhq crossmatch runs/tess-pi-men-s1' when the archive answers.

crossmatch_line: Host of published planet pi Men c (P 6.268 d)

calibration.source: Per-reviewer rates printed by 'exoplan calibrate' when it wrote reviewer_weights_full_panel.json on 2026-10-16. Sample size from the commit that added the weights: n = 10 injected and 10 empty subjects per reviewer.

attribution: Sentinels run on Claude (Anthropic) by default; other providers are supported and labelled. Probes are deterministic matched-filter detectors.
